events.body: The following sections might be updated with supplementary metadata relevant to reviewers and maintainers. ### External sites * Code coverage & benchmarks: https://corecheck.dev/bitcoin/bitcoin/pulls/36696 * Ralph review https://git.fish.foo/bitcoin/bitcoin/pulls/36696#author-ralph ### Reviews See [the guideline](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-review) and [AI policy](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/AI_POLICY.md) for information on the review process. | Type | Reviewers | | ---- | --------- | | Concept ACK | [sedited](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36696#issuecomment-6631621595) | If your review is incorrectly listed, please copy-paste <!--meta-tag:bot-skip--> into the comment that the bot should ignore. ### Conflicts Reviewers, this pull request conflicts with the following ones: * [#36543](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36543) (validation: check the most recent AssumeUTXO commitment during IBD by l0rinc) If you consider this pull request important, please also help to review the conflicting pull requests. Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.
The `CTxIn` witness argument is a nice addition. It would remove the “assign the witness after replacing vin” workaround I needed in several places in #36606 and #36694.

I have replaced the commits that exemplify the constructor in action with one that shows multiple things in a single place:

- It shows the new constructor of `CTransaction` in action.
- It shows the new constructor of `CTxIn` in action.
- It shows how `CMutableTransaction` is not necessary in many places, not just for building, but also as function argument.
- It reveals `GetTxSigOpCost` as an example test that contains multiple blocks where each should become its own unit test.
- It reveals potential test dependencies: Each test setup modifies the `CCoinsViewCache`. It is not clear whether a test might depend on the modifications of tests run earlier or not.
- It shows that `CTransaction` could benefit from applying best practices (never use `const` data members, maintain immutability by not providing write access): In `return {std::move(creationTx), std::move(spendingTx)};`, the compiler provided move constructor of `CTransaction` invokes the move constructors of all its data members, which are `const`, so they fall back to copying (this does not fire `performance-move-const-arg`, because the individual data members fall back, not the tx object).
- It reveals the annoyance that `CTransaction` does not provide regular semantics: It is not possible to replace the existing values with `std::tie(creationTx, spendingTx) = BuildTxs(...);`, because `CTransaction` is only sort-of copyable (due to not following ... I repeat myself. This is not a big deal here, as tests should be refactored for independence anyway).
- It also provides an example where code could be much less verbose if the constructor accepted `std::vector` and explicit types were not required at the call site, and why I claim this to be less readable:

```cpp
CTransaction creationTx{{{{}}}, {{1, scriptPubKey}}, 1};
CTransaction spendingTx{{{{creationTx.GetHash(), 0}, scriptSig, CTxIn::SEQUENCE_FINAL, witness}}, {{1, {}}}, 1};
```

comments.body: nit: I'd still prefer the easier C++11 std::vector here (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36692#issuecomment-6501722895) but I'll leave it to other reviewers to decide.

```suggestion
    if constexpr (std::is_lvalue_reference_v<R> || std::ranges::view<std::remove_cvref_t<R>>) {
```

I think `std::span{inputs}` would still move the elements out of `inputs`. Copying for views avoids that. What do you think?

```suggestion
    explicit CTransaction(In&& in, Out&& out, uint32_t ver = CURRENT_VERSION, uint32_t lt = 0)
```
Should this be explicit like the existing ones?

That is a good point. I think we should just invoke `std::ranges::copy` unconditionally. In C++23, we can remove this helper and use tag dispatching with `std::from_range`. All as long as we actually want range support, so I will leave this open until https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36696#discussion_r4415029088 is resolved.
Implicit conversion cannot happen because the constructor requires at least two arguments.
Fixed it. Instead of moving when `R` is an rvalue, we want to move when R *yields* rvalues. `std::ranges::copy` already does that and so does `std::from_range`.
